whyThisIsCorrectBehaviourNotADefect: This is GK-SEC-004 working as designed. The committed delegation is read from git and is scoped to BOTH projectId 'projectos' AND programme 'projectos-autonomous-self-hosting'; its own text states it cannot be read as authority in any other project or programme. A fresh witness therefore has no decider, and nothing in the runtime will invent one. Deliberately reusing the ProjectOS programme or project id to borrow that authority would be precisely the cross-project leakage the design forbids, and was not done.
ownerGatedPrerequisitesDiscovered: An owner-approved PLAN for the witness project. Plan approval is owner-gated and no plan-approval delegation exists for this programme.

A COMMITTED gatekeeper delegation at .projectops/authority/closure-delegation.json with programmeScope 'projectos-degraded-witness2' and delegatedTo naming a decider. Delegation is the owner delegating TO ChatGPT; ChatGPT cannot delegate authority to itself.
Only after those two can the runtime attempt the transport, classify unavailability and derive the GKOUT identity that the degraded grant must bind to.
Then the one-use degraded grant itself — the gate that was anticipated.
consequence: The anticipated single owner gate is in fact preceded by two further owner-gated prerequisites. That materially changes the cost and shape of witness2, and it is a governance-design decision rather than an implementation choice, so it returns to the gatekeeper rather than being resolved by the implementer.
